case_study_insert.main_stem: Vantage Digital Platforms (VDP) is a cooperative in the e-commerce sector, employing a workforce of 65. Founded in 2012 by Aisha Bello, it runs an online marketplace for small retailers and operates a flat structure with autocratic leadership. VDP plans to invest $600,000 in a new automated fulfilment warehouse with digital stock control, financed by a $350,000 bank loan and $250,000 from the sale of assets. It has fixed costs of $390,000 a year, a variable cost of $13.00 a unit and a selling price of $28.00, and currently produces 75,000 units a year. VDP faces two problems: a 2.7% pick-error rate and 24 of 65 staff lacking digital stock-control training.
case_study_insert.appendix_1_marketing_ops: E-commerce Operations Log — Q4 2025: VDP fulfilled 28,000 online orders; the pick-error rate was 2.7%, down from 4.1% a year earlier. Customer complaints fell from 175 to 88 per month. Average delivery time is 2.6 days. A survey of 640 shoppers found 62% prefer free returns and 55% buy mainly on mobile. A skills audit shows 24 of 65 staff lack digital stock-control training; a training course costs $980 per employee.

appendix_2_financial_data.title: Extract from the Statement of Profit or Loss and Capital employed data of Vantage Digital Platforms for the year ended 31 March 2025 ($ '000)

case_study_insert.appendix_3_external_environment: Economic and Retail Bulletin (September 2026): (1) The base interest rate rose from 4.0% to 4.75%, increasing borrowing costs on variable-rate loans. (2) The national minimum wage increased by 6.9% to $13.45 an hour from April 2026. (3) Packaging and delivery input costs rose 9.4% year-on-year, while online retail sales grew 5.2% over the same period.

questions.question_text: VDP plans to fund part of its $600,000 automated warehouse with a bank loan. Explain two advantages for VDP of using the bank loan rather than the sale of assets.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: A bank loan lets VDP keep the assets it would otherwise sell, so the cooperative retains the resources needed to run its marketplace while investing $350,000 of the $600,000 in the automated warehouse. Selling assets would reduce the capacity serving 75,000 units, whereas the loan preserves the asset base that supports the 2.7% pick-error improvement programme.

Point 2: A loan provides the full sum immediately and can be repaid over time, while a sale of assets may take months and fetch less than expected in a downturn. This certainty helps Aisha Bello commit to digital stock control and training at $980 per employee for 24 staff without delaying the project. It leaves the 65-member cooperative in control of operations, provided the $390,000 fixed costs and interest can be met. With packaging and delivery costs expected to rise 9.4%, avoiding an asset sale also keeps the cooperative's earning assets in place to absorb that pressure.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid advantage identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for contextual explanation and analysis applied to VDP's financing choice, operations and warehouse investment.

questions.question_text: VDP is promoting its marketplace to new shoppers. Consider paid social media advertising, email marketing to existing shoppers, or discount vouchers with influencers. Which should VDP choose? Justify your recommendation.
questions.model_answer:
Paid social media advertising: Social ads can reach many shoppers quickly and can target the 55% of the 640 surveyed who buy mainly on mobile. They are measurable but costs rise with competition and results depend on creative quality; for a cooperative committing $600,000 to a warehouse and servicing a $350,000 loan, unmeasured spend would be risky.

Email marketing to existing shoppers: Email is cheap, directly reaches known customers and can highlight the free returns wanted by 62% of respondents and faster delivery from the new warehouse. It is readily measurable through open and click rates. Its limitation is that it cannot reach new shoppers beyond the existing list, so it may not grow the 75,000-unit base on its own.

Discount vouchers with influencers: Influencer vouchers can create buzz and attract new, younger shoppers, and can be tied to 62% preferring free returns. However, discounts cut the $28.00 price and $15.00 contribution, influencer fees are uncertain, and a 65-person cooperative has little experience managing such campaigns.

Recommendation: VDP should choose email marketing to existing shoppers. It is low-cost, measurable and matches the research insight that 62% want free returns and 55% buy on mobile, with funds better kept for the $600,000 warehouse. Paid social is rejected as competitive and costly; influencer vouchers are rejected because discounts would erode contribution needed to cover $390,000 fixed costs and the bank loan. Email also suits a cooperative whose 65 members value direct communication, and it can promote free returns to the 62% who want them without discounting the $28.00 price.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Lists or describes promotional options with limited application to VDP.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Discusses advantages and disadvantages of at least two options in VDP's context with some judgement.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Evaluates all three options in VDP's context and gives a justified recommendation explaining why social advertising and influencer vouchers are rejected.

questions.question_text: VDP has a 2.7% pick-error rate and 24 of its 65 staff lack digital stock-control training. Explain two benefits for VDP of using autocratic leadership in the warehouse.
questions.model_answer:
Point 1: Autocratic leadership sets one clear picking procedure for all staff, directly targeting the 2.7% pick-error rate, down from 4.1% a year earlier, and helping complaints stay below 88 per month. In a flat structure, Aisha Bello can issue unambiguous instructions and correct mistakes at once, which matters when digital stock control is being introduced in the $600,000 warehouse and 2.6-day delivery must be protected.

Point 2: Centralised decisions allow quick allocation of the $980 training courses to the 24 untrained staff and firm enforcement of stock-control rules, supporting the 62% of surveyed shoppers who want free returns. Clear direction reduces confusion among a workforce of 65 and speeds adaptation to the 55% of shoppers buying on mobile, while the $350,000 loan is being serviced. Clear instructions also protect the 2.6-day delivery promise when 55% of shoppers buy on mobile and expect fast, accurate order fulfilment. Order accuracy therefore protects both member goodwill and the cooperative's profitability.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for each valid benefit identified (max 2).
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for detailed contextual development linked to VDP's pick errors, training gap and warehouse investment.

questions.question_text: VDP must train 24 staff in digital stock control. Consider on-the-job coaching or external training at $980 per employee. Which should VDP choose? Justify your decision.
questions.model_answer:
On-the-job coaching: Training alongside the new warehouse systems is specific to VDP's own stock-control software, costs no fees and keeps all 24 staff fulfilling orders, protecting the 75,000-unit base and the 2.6-day delivery time. Supervisors can demonstrate the exact picking routines behind the fall from 4.1% to 2.7% errors. However, trainers may not be fully trained themselves, bad habits can spread and no certificate is given, which is a concern for a cooperative expanding its digital systems.

External training: A formal course gives structured, up-to-date stock-control skills and a recognised qualification. For 24 staff the fee is 24 × $980 = $23,520, an explicit calculation from the insert, affordable against the $250,000 asset-sale proceeds. Staff are absent from the warehouse temporarily and generic content may not match VDP's software, so follow-up coaching would still be needed.

Decision: VDP should choose on-the-job coaching, with a short external course for the warehouse supervisors. Coaching is cheaper, system-specific and avoids withdrawing 24 staff from order fulfilment while the $600,000 warehouse opens. External training for all is rejected because the $23,520 fee and lost picking time would threaten the 2.7% error-rate improvement and 2.6-day delivery, and the skills can be taught on site where the equipment is. Because the cooperative's warehouse is new, managers can coach staff on the exact software rather than a generic course. The $23,520 saved can instead improve the 2.6-day delivery service that 55% of mobile shoppers expect, and on-the-job coaching can be delivered in shifts so no staff are absent from picking.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Basic description of the two training methods with limited application to VDP.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Detailed analysis of benefits and drawbacks of both methods in VDP's context.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Comprehensive evaluation of both methods with a justified decision covering cost, disruption and system relevance, rejecting the alternative.

questions.question_text: Calculate and explain how VDP's management can use its cost, break-even and productivity data.

sub_parts.model_answer: Formula: Break-even output = Fixed costs ÷ Contribution per unit. Substitution: $390,000 ÷ ($28.00 − $13.00) = $390,000 ÷ $15.00 = 26,000 units. Answer: break-even output is 26,000 units a year.
Formula: Contribution per unit = Selling price − Variable cost per unit. Substitution: $28.00 − $13.00 = $15.00. Answer: contribution per unit is $15.00.

sub_parts.question_text: Explain four ways VDP's management can use this financial data.
sub_parts.model_answer:
1. Compare the 26,000-unit break-even output with 75,000 units fulfilled to find a margin of safety of 49,000 units, showing how much demand can fall before the $600,000 warehouse becomes loss-making.
2. Use $15.00 contribution to price free-returns offers: an extra $1.00 of delivery cost leaves $14.00, so managers can calculate the extra orders needed to keep covering $390,000 fixed costs.
3. Check that 75,000 × $15.00 = $1,125,000 contribution covers $390,000 fixed costs and interest on the $350,000 bank loan, informing whether further borrowing is prudent.
4. Benchmark unit cost ($390,000 ÷ 75,000 = $5.20 plus $13.00 = $18.20 a unit) against the 9.4% packaging and delivery inflation and link it to the 2.7% pick-error rate and 2.6-day delivery time.

questions.model_answer: (i) Break-even output = 26,000 units | (ii) Contribution per unit = $15.00 | (iii) Four contextual uses explained: margin of safety of 49,000 units against 75,000-unit output; free-returns pricing with $390,000 fixed costs; loan feasibility on the $350,000 bank loan; and unit-cost benchmarking at $18.20 against 9.4% input inflation.

working_marks: 1 mark for correct formula/method, 1 mark for accurate numerical answer in (i) and (ii). 1 mark per valid applied point in (iii).

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 2, evaluate VDP's profitability by calculating the gross profit margin, profit margin and return on capital employed for 2024 and 2025. Has VDP's profitability improved? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Calculations:
Gross Profit Margin 2024 = 45.0%
Gross Profit Margin 2025 = 50.0%
Profit Margin 2024 = 17.5%
Profit Margin 2025 = 22.0%
ROCE 2024 = 14.0%
ROCE 2025 = 20.0%

Detailed workings: 2024 gross profit $720 ÷ revenue $1,600 = 45.0%; 2025 gross profit $1,000 ÷ revenue $2,000 = 50.0%. Operating profit 2024 $280 ÷ revenue $1,600 = 17.5%; 2025 $440 ÷ revenue $2,000 = 22.0%. Operating profit 2024 $280 ÷ capital employed $2,000 = 14.0%; 2025 $440 ÷ capital employed $2,200 = 20.0%. Revenue grew from $1,600 to $2,000 while cost of sales rose only from $880 to $1,000, so gross profit rose much faster than sales.

Evaluation: Profitability improved on every measure. The higher gross percentage shows stronger control of direct fulfilment costs relative to revenue, consistent with a $28.00 price and $13.00 variable cost on 75,000 units. The operating percentage rose from 17.5% to 22.0% because operating profit grew from $280 to $440 faster than revenue, showing $390,000 fixed costs were spread over more orders. The return on capital climbed from 14.0% to 20.0%, so the slightly larger $2,200 capital base is working far harder, supporting the $600,000 warehouse. Interest payable rose from $45 to $60 but is small against $440 operating profit.

Conclusion: VDP's profitability has improved: all three measures rose together and the gain comes from revenue growth and cost control rather than asset sales. The caution is that a variable-rate $350,000 loan and a 2.7% pick-error rate could erode the 50.0% gross percentage, so the cooperative should protect accuracy while expanding fulfilment.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: States financial figures or changes without accurate ratio calculations.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Accurately calculates the gross profit margin, profit margin and ROCE for both years with contextual analysis of the trend.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Accurate calculations for both years combined with detailed evaluation of revenue, cost and capital movements and a justified conclusion on profitability.

questions.question_text: Explain one advantage and one disadvantage for VDP of introducing digital stock control in its fulfilment warehouse.
questions.model_answer:
Advantage: Digital stock control directly reduces the 2.7% pick-error rate, down from 4.1% a year earlier, by tracking inventory accurately and guiding picking. Fewer errors keep complaints below the current 88 per month and support the 62% of the 640 surveyed shoppers who want free returns and the 55% who buy on mobile, protecting the $28.00 price and $15.00 contribution on 75,000 units.

Disadvantage: The system is part of the $600,000 warehouse investment and could raise the $390,000 fixed costs, increasing the 26,000-unit break-even output. It also relies on skills that 24 of 65 staff lack, so initial configuration errors or over-dependence on software could disrupt the 2.6-day delivery time while the $350,000 bank loan is being repaid. VDP can measure success directly against the 28,000 orders fulfilled last quarter and the fall in complaints to 88 per month, so the benefit of stock control is verified rather than assumed.

knowledge_max_2: 1 mark for a valid advantage and 1 mark for a valid disadvantage.
application_analysis_max_6: Up to 3 marks per point for detailed contextual development linked to VDP's pick-error rate, research data, costs and skills.

questions.question_text: Using Appendix 3, evaluate how the interest rate rise to 4.75%, the 6.9% minimum wage increase to $13.45 and the 9.4% rise in packaging and delivery costs will affect VDP. Which change will have the greatest impact? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer:
Interest rate rise (4.0% to 4.75%): If VDP's $350,000 bank loan is variable-rate, the extra interest is 0.75% × $350,000 = $2,625 a year (0.0075 × $350,000). That is modest beside $390,000 fixed costs and $440 of operating profit, and the $250,000 raised from asset sales reduces the need for further borrowing. VDP could also fix the loan rate, so the direct effect is contained.

Minimum wage increase (6.9% to $13.45): The insert gives a workforce of 65 but not the hours worked or the number of minimum-wage staff, so no annual wage bill can be invented. The defensible judgement is qualitative: a 6.9% rise increases unit labour cost unless productivity holds at 75,000 ÷ 65 = about 1,154 units per employee, and the digital stock-control gap among 24 staff makes that harder. It makes the $980 training course relatively more worthwhile.

Packaging and delivery input inflation (9.4%): The insert gives a variable cost of $13.00 a unit without decomposing it. A labelled upper bound if the whole variable cost rose 9.4% is 0.094 × $13.00 = $1.222 a unit; across 75,000 units that is 75,000 × $1.222 = $91,650 a year, cutting contribution from $15.00 to $13.78. Even partial pass-through would reduce the surplus covering $390,000 fixed costs.

Conclusion: The 9.4% rise in packaging and delivery costs will have the greatest impact. It applies to every order, can add $91,650 a year on the stated assumption and directly erodes the $15.00 contribution funding the $600,000 warehouse; the interest rise is only $2,625 and the wage effect cannot be quantified from the insert and can be offset by maintaining productivity.

mark_scheme.level_1_1_to_4: Identifies the external changes with limited application to VDP.
mark_scheme.level_2_5_to_8: Analyses the impact of at least two external changes on VDP's costs, revenue or financing in context.
mark_scheme.level_3_9_to_12: Detailed evaluation of all three changes in VDP's context with justified greatest-impact judgement and shown derivations, rejecting the smaller effects.
